title: n8n vs Zapier vs Make: Which Automation Tool Should Your Business Choose in 2026?
summary: An honest comparison of n8n, Zapier and Make for businesses: ease of use, pricing models, AI agents, data control and scalability, with recommendations by use case.
body:
n8n, Zapier and Make are the three most popular tools for automating business workflows. All three connect your apps and can add AI to your processes, but they suit different needs. Here is a practical comparison to help you choose.

## The short answer

- Choose **Zapier** for quick, simple automations set up by non-technical teams.
- Choose **Make** for visual multi-step scenarios at a moderate cost.
- Choose **n8n** for complex workflows, AI agents, high volumes or when you want control over your data.

![n8n, Zapier and Make compared at a glance](/images/blog/n8n-vs-zapier-vs-make-table.webp)

## Zapier

**Strengths**: the easiest to learn, the largest catalogue of app integrations, and plenty of templates. A marketing or sales team can build useful automations in minutes.

**Limits**: pricing is based on tasks, so costs rise quickly as volumes grow. Complex logic, loops and data transformations are possible but less comfortable. Data is processed in Zapier's cloud only.

**Best for**: small teams, simple "when this happens, do that" automations, quick wins.

## Make

**Strengths**: a very visual editor where you see data flow through each step. Good handling of routers, filters and iterations, at a lower cost than Zapier for many use cases.

**Limits**: pricing is per operation, which can add up with large datasets. Very advanced logic or custom code is more limited than in n8n. Cloud only.

**Best for**: teams that want powerful visual scenarios without writing code.

## n8n

**Strengths**: the most flexible of the three. You can mix visual nodes with JavaScript or Python, call any API, and build **AI agents** with memory, tools and vector databases natively. It can run in the cloud or be **self-hosted** on your own server, which helps with privacy rules and keeps costs predictable at high volume.

**Limits**: a steeper learning curve, and self-hosting means you are responsible for updates, backups and security (or a partner is).

**Best for**: complex processes, AI automation, high volumes, and businesses that care about data control.

## Pricing models compared

- **Zapier**: per task (each action that runs).
- **Make**: per operation (each module that runs).
- **n8n**: per workflow execution on the cloud plans, or your own server cost when self-hosted.

For a workflow with many steps that runs thousands of times a month, the difference between counting each step and counting each execution can be very large. Always estimate your monthly volume before choosing.

## Which one for AI automation?

All three now offer AI features. For simple uses (summarise an e-mail, draft a reply), any of them works. For **AI agents** that reason, use several tools and keep context, n8n currently offers the most control and flexibility.

## Our recommendation by use case

- **Sync form leads to a CRM and send a welcome e-mail**: Zapier or Make.
- **Multi-step order processing with filters and branches**: Make or n8n.
- **Invoice reminders, reporting and document processing at scale**: n8n.
- **AI agent answering customers from your own data**: n8n.
- **Strict data privacy requirements**: self-hosted n8n.
